feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and good evidence of scope across web, content, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition, and tighter structure across overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support “Digital Communications & Strategy Lead.”  
- Strong credibility: NACo progression shows advancement and ownership of substantial platforms, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration and analytics modernization.  
- Writing is polished and mostly error-free, with concise, professional phrasing and good use of specifics.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope: include percentage growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, cost savings, campaign results, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve scannability and save space.  
- Minor style/consistency edits: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience”; add the serial comma consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “workflows and systems”); standardize hyphenation such as “organization-wide” and “member-facing.” No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and anchoring it more directly to recent leadership and platform modernization work would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Add stronger specificity from recent roles, such as enterprise web transformation, cross-channel governance, and analytics-enabled decision-making.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, enterprise web modernization, editorial workflow design, and digital governance. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into accessible content, aligning stakeholders across teams, and building systems that improve coordination, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is already well supported in work experience; avoid overloading the intro with similar phrasing.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It will be more effective if tightened to emphasize senior-level strengths and reduce generic phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad terms with sharper, higher-value language: “Digital transformation & platform modernization,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Align wording with the strongest evidence in recent roles: web/CMS modernization, analytics infrastructure, advocacy communications, and multimedia/event production.
- Reduce filler like “multi-channel communication” and “stakeholder & cross-department coordination,” which read more generic than differentiating.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation & platform modernization • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platforms & CMS administration • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, reporting & insight generation • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; keep this section concise and higher-level rather than repeating exact categories.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance to your headline, but it reads broad and overlaps with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around scope, seniority, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets and lead with impact: combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on enterprise communications operations.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams enabled, search/discovery improvements, or efficiency gains.
- Rephrase technical bullet to emphasize business value: “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components that improved launch speed, content reuse, and member access to resources.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet high-level or add a distinct outcome.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language closely echoes the NACo Director role; differentiate by stressing consulting/embedded leadership and current delivery.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive wins first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Make channel oversight more outcome-driven: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with stronger metrics if available (subscriber growth, engagement, open rates, campaign results).
- Condense into 4–5 bullets, e.g.:
- Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy, events, and recurring multimedia programming.
- Expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve reporting and decision-making.
- Established stronger digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role’s newsletter/social/video management.
- Video-programming language may duplicate the footer project list; keep this entry focused on leadership and scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution with impact: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams around more consistent digital production processes.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “strengthened workflows/governance” language already used in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinctive by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad terms with tighter, higher-signal language:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content governance & planning” if you want to stress systems over editorial execution.
- If space allows, align wording to recent experience by using “enterprise web modernization” or “digital governance” rather than generic “digital strategy.”
- Keep parallel structure: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat ideas already stated in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is close to “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one phrasing consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, make it more outcome-oriented and emphasize the most relevant, recent capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are central to target roles; they can stay in “Technical + IT.”
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based operational systems” or “workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “supporting large public-facing sites and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full platform lists below.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies—avoid repeating exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools after the strategic skills: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten wording and group related items: “KPI design & dashboarding” and “Executive/leadership reporting” instead of separate fragmented terms
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive reporting & dashboarding • SEO and digital performance analysis • GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly
- Avoid repeating every analytics tool here if they are already listed elsewhere; use this section to signal senior-level strengths instead

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section above. This item should either be tightened or reframed to emphasize depth in the most relevant platforms, especially Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by relevance/recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level: “Drupal (advanced) • WordPress (admin/build) • SharePoint (content/intranet) • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing.
- If Drupal is your strongest differentiator, place it first and consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s not materially important.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already includes Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor relative to your enterprise/public-sector platform leadership unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and slightly more current/senior.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery
- Add specificity by grouping tools by use case: Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, replace older/general terms with stronger phrasing: “custom front-end development,” “serverless scripting,” or “deployment automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless they matter; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one section broader and this one more tool-specific
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid adding it here unless tied to GitHub Actions or API work specifically

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too long and mixes automation platforms with collaboration/project tools. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and prioritize true automation tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier” | “Jira • Asana • Trello” | “Slack • Teams”.
- Drop Basecamp unless it was materially used in recent roles; it reads older/less relevant than the others.
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Project & Collaboration Tools” so the list matches the category.
- If space allows, add light specificity instead of more tools: “Airtable workflow design • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello • Slack/Teams”.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are generic unless tied to workflow coordination; keep only if they support the systems narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this line is too generic and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent NACo roles. Tightening the label and ordering by strongest/recentest platform would make it feel more intentional.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Reorder for likely relevance/recency: Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just tool names, e.g. “Higher Logic (newsletter/member communications)” and “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation/segmentation)”
- Keep to 2–3 platforms only; if one was lightly used, remove it rather than listing everything

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work bullets about email/newsletters; keep this strictly platform-focused, not responsibility-focused
- Avoid adding analytics or automation tools here; those are already covered in other Technical + IT sections

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Tighten phrasing and specify channels/results: “supported web, email, social, livestream, and video operations” instead of “strengthening workflows across…”
- Add concrete outputs if available: number of livestreams/events produced, cadence of weekly videos, website size/traffic at refresh, or team/process improvements.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported day-to-day web, email, social, livestream, and video operations; contributed to a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; and provided functional guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on launching/building the capability.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; use more junior, execution-oriented language here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Good foundation, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since this is an older role, keep it concise and frame it as an early signal of digital/multimedia leadership.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- Tighten the rest into one supporting clause: “Coordinated innovation and research projects that supported program initiatives and policy communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational programs.”
- If possible, add one metric or scope point: episode count, audience, number of projects supported, or cross-team stakeholders.

Possible rewrite
- Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting NACo program initiatives and policy communications, while producing digital and multimedia content for organizational priorities.
- Launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing broad multimedia leadership here; later NACo roles already cover video, digital operations and channel management in more depth.
